definitions.gloss: red bean rice; glutinous rice steamed with azuki beans
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese dish of glutinous rice (もち米) steamed with red azuki beans, giving it a distinctive pinkish-red color. Served at celebrations and auspicious occasions.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{祝|いわ}い→お祝い：01339_oiwai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{赤飯|せきはん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{炊|た}いた→炊く：02127_taku⟧。
⟦{七五三|しちごさん}→七五三：06185_shichigosan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{祝|いわ}い→お祝い：01339_oiwai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{赤飯|せきはん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{配|くば}った→配る：03921_kubaru⟧。
examples.english: We handed out sekihan for the Shichi-Go-San celebration.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{孫|まご}→孫：03731_mago⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{入学|にゅうがく}→入学：02092_nyuugaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{祝|いわ}って→祝う：01881_iwau⟧、⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{赤飯|せきはん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{蒸|む}して→蒸す：02307_musu⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother steamed sekihan from early morning to celebrate her grandchild's school admission.

notes: Literally 'red rice,' composed of {赤|せき} (red) + {飯|はん} (cooked rice). The red color, from the azuki beans, symbolizes good luck and is associated with celebrations in Japanese culture. Traditionally prepared for occasions such as birthdays, weddings, ⟦{七五三|しちごさん}→七五三：06185_shichigosan⟧ (children's milestone festival), school entrance ceremonies, and other happy events. Also called お{赤飯|せきはん} with the polite prefix お. Available as instant packs in supermarkets and convenience stores.
